analysis.title: USA: Core Capital Goods Orders in Line With Expectations but Shipments Above Expectations; Boosting Q3 GDP Tracking Estimate to 3.4%
key_insights: September durable goods orders rose 1.8% MoM, roughly in line with the 1.9% median forecast. The increase largely reflects commercial aircraft orders.
Durable goods ex-transportation rose 0.5% MoM and core capital goods orders rose 0.5% MoM, both roughly in line with expectations. Computers and related products and machinery drove the gains.
Core capital goods shipments rose 1.2% MoM versus the GS forecast of +1.0% and the median forecast of +0.8%, above expectations.
August was revised up: durable goods orders +0.2pp to +0.1%, ex-transportation +0.1pp to +0.3%, core capital goods shipments +0.1pp to +0.6%. Manufacturing inventories rose 0.4%.

Core capital goods shipments and the inventory details were slightly stronger than GS's previous GDP tracking assumptions. GS raised its Q3 GDP tracking estimate by 0.1pp to +3.4% (quarter-over-quarter annualized).
